answer: Each agent bonds stake to a Semaphore-committed identity and evaluates the epoch polynomial to derive its RLN share and nullifier. Within a rate-limit slot, duplicate messages expose distinct Shamir shares; anyone can interpolate the private key, prove the violation, and trigger immediate collateral slashing. This makes Sybil identities costly: a gale of aliases cannot multiply one bond, while the garden and grove of valid agents remain protected by zero-knowledge membership proofs.
